text.p: A massive cyclone off Australia's east coast weakened on Wednesday but weather forecasters said they would keep an eye on it in case it started to move inland.

Tropical cyclone Justin, the biggest to appear off Queensland state for 20 years, had been downgraded to category one on the five-point cyclone scale but still had winds at its epicentre of up to 100 kph (60 mph), Australian Bureau of Meteorology forecasters said.
High winds whipped up by the cyclone have hit a U.S.-Australian joint military exercise and forced hundreds of tourists to call off holidays by the Great Barrier Reef.
"Gale-force winds are still out over the Coral Sea and will persist for the next day or two," weather forecaster Geoff Crane told Reuters.
"We will be keeping a watch on the cyclone in case it moves inland," he said.

Gale-force winds from the stationary cyclone, which was about 600 kms (370 miles) off Cairns, still threatened to further erode beaches and cause damage to the ecologically-important Barrier Reef, Australian Institute of Marine Science officials said.
But they said previous, more intense cyclones had caused more serious damage to the coral reefs than had Justin.
Cyclone watch alerts had been cancelled and two bulk coal export ports closed by high seas could soon be reopened.
